concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 9 – Data hygiene & reproducibility utilities – T013
concerns.text: Task T013 (Data hygiene) is placed after the contract‑validation task T011. Since T011 validates all artifacts against the schemas, it expects the checksum metadata to already be present. Running T013 later means the metadata may be missing during validation, violating the producer‑before‑consumer ordering rule.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 9 – Data hygiene & reproducibility utilities – T014
concerns.text: Task T014 (Reproducibility: pinned seeds) is scheduled after many stochastic tasks (T002, T003, T004, T005, T007). The seed definition must exist before any task that relies on randomness, otherwise those tasks cannot guarantee reproducibility. This ordering breaks the foundational‑tasks‑first principle.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 0 – Project scaffolding & early sanity check – T001
concerns.text: Task T001 is marked `[P?]` but writes files into `code/` and `quickstart.md`. If other tasks were executed in parallel and also write to the `code/` directory, a race condition could arise. The `[P]` safety tag should be removed or the task should be explicitly serialized.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Phase 0 – Project scaffolding & early sanity check – T002
concerns.text: Task T002 is also marked `[P?]` and writes `results/power_report.md`. Parallel execution with other tasks that write to the `results/` directory could cause file‑write conflicts. Clarify that this task is not parallel‑safe or adjust the tag.
